pr_title: Change USR1 so it actually stops after work has been completed.
pr_comments:
Added usr1_shutdown branch.
I believe the problem now is that the Launcher actor thread is locked forever, waiting on manager's :shutdown signal.  Actors typically can only process one message at a time, so TERM's stop message won't process until USR1's stop message processing returns.
Cleaned up the USR1 signal processing a bit.
Hm. Yeah, maybe I'll just make the Manager exit(0). I'll have to do some
handling around the watchdog since it catches the exception and logs it. I
might not get to this today but will try to tomorrow.

issue_context.title: workers don't exit after USR1 signal
issue_context.body:
If I understand correctly, the USR1 signal should cause a worker to stop accepting jobs and then to exit when it has completed what it is working on.  After sending kill -USR1 I see that the worker stops accepting jobs but then it never exits.   This is what I see in the process list: "sidekiq 2.17.0 Project [0 of 1 busy]"

This is on Ubuntu 12.04.1 LTS, running ruby ruby 2.0.0p353, rails 3.2.12, sidekiq-pro 1.3.2

Thanks

Alex

This is because the USR1 doesn't actually cause the launcher to stop and exit(0). If you trace the code paths, the TERM raises an Interrupt which is rescued, and stops the launcher and `exit(0)`. The USR1 code path simply stops the actors, the `signal(:shutdown)` in `shutdown` doesn't stop the process, just sends a message to waiting methods. Since there is no one waiting, e.g,. no `manager.wait(:shutdown)` waiting code, nothing happens.

I can fix this in a pull later today.
@mperham check out https://github.com/mperham/sidekiq/pull/1387
@alexfarrill Both @mperham and I were unable to get this working within reasonable timeboxes in #1387. I'm going to update the changelog to remove the line which says that USR1 exits after stopping. I confirmed that the wiki still says that USR1 only stops workers, it does not exit the program.
Thanks Jonathan and Mike for giving this a shot, if I have some time to
experiment with this later this month I will also give it a try.

This has been motivated by the use case of a long running worker (~30
minute jobs) that we don't want to kill or wait to complete during
deployment.  For this worker, operating on its own queue, I am working on a
different solution: we don't kill the worker during deploy and we call exit
at the end of the perform method.  The idea is that the process will then
be restarted by upstart or monit every time it runs and so will never be
interrupted by deploying but will always have the latest code on the next
run.  I think this pattern gives us a good workaround for this.

Alex

review_comments:
I believe the main thread will wait here forever if a worker does not shutdown.  Then the TERM signal will not be handled and Sidekiq will need to be force killed.  Can you test a USR1 which does not exit early and verify TERM still works?
You're right: it does block the main thread. What are your thoughts here? Moving `exit(0)` into the Manager instead of signaling a shutdown could do this, though it's less desirable from a design standpoint. I Googled a bit to see if there was a good way to set up some kind of callback, but all the signaling seemed to invoke `wait` under the hood and block the thread.
Why not just have the manager call exit when all workers are quiet?  No need to defer to the main thread, afaik.
Yeah, that's the only solution I could see. I think it's less desirable from a design perspective since the manager is also handling process control. I'll give it a try tomorrow and see how it turns out.
I just pushed up a change to move the `exit(0)` into the `Launcher`. From testing it out, it allows you to send a USR1 followed by a TERM because the `wait` now happens async. Note that I updated the Interrupt handling to now do `launcher.async.stop` (which allows USR1 and TERM to share the same code path while not blocking each other). It appears to work AFAICT from testing it out.

I can't code more tonight but can finish up any other modifications you have tomorrow.
No problem, in the future can you use a branch in the main sidekiq repo so I can work on the branch too before merging?
Oh, yeah definitely. Never been added as a repo collaborator before, will
do going forward.
